notation: WCA/SiGN outer-block notation: R U F L D B, primes ', doubles 2; wide moves lowercase (r, u, f...); slices M E S; rotations x y z
conventions: Cross on D (white bottom). 'front-colour' = colour of the F centre, 'right-colour' = colour of the R centre (green/red in the standard white-bottom, green-front scheme).

Case numbering and canonical case state follow SpeedCubeDB F2L 1-41 (https://www.speedcubedb.com/a/3x3/F2L). The speedsolving.com wiki uses the same numbers for 1-36; the wiki inserts a 'Solved' entry as F2L 37, so wiki F2L 38-42 = F2L 37-41 here (see speedsolving_wiki_number).

Every alg in a case solves the IDENTICAL case state (same corner/edge positions and orientations including the U-layer position, not just up to AUF). Case state = inverse(alg) applied to a solved cube. Leading U/U'/U2 moves in algs are part of the published solution for that canonical state (the pieces are not pre-aligned), not an added AUF.

No alg contains x/y/z rotations; algs using d/u moves that leave the cross displaced were dropped (they are disguised rotations). Algs that use other slots temporarily (e.g. F' L' U2 L F, R B U2 B' R') restore them.
Text normalisation vs sources: grouping parentheses removed, X2' written as X2, and repeat groups like (R' F R F')2 expanded (noted in alg_notes). Moves otherwise verbatim.

All algs were checked with an independent sticker simulator: inverse(alg) on a solved cube leaves cross + FL/BL/BR slots + centres intact, and all algs of one case produce the same FR corner/edge state.
